evidence.quote: description: 'Manage n8n credentials. Actions: list, get, create, update, delete, getSchema. Use getSchema to discover required fields before creating. SECURITY: credential data values are never logged.',

reason: Ordinary usage guidance for the tool's own purpose (list actions, call getSchema before create); it does not tell the model to read secrets, call other tools, send data out or hide anything. The word 'credentials' is just the tool's subject.
fix: None needed for the description (see M001 for the actual logging problem).

reason: Inside the GET / info handler the host value is only used to build the displayed base URL; it does not bind a socket. The real listen call is F003.

The HTTP server binds all interfaces by default, but every MCP endpoint (/mcp GET/POST/DELETE, /sse, /messages) calls authenticateRequest with a timing-safe bearer-token check and startup refuses an empty token. Whether all-interface exposure is acceptable depends on the deployment (container behind a proxy vs. a laptop).
fix: Default HOST to 127.0.0.1 for non-container runs and document setting HOST=0.0.0.0 only behind TLS/reverse proxy.

reason: Display-only value inside the GET / info handler; no socket is bound here (the listen call is F005).
Legacy HTTP server binds all interfaces by default; POST /mcp requires a timing-safe bearer token, so exposure risk depends on where it is deployed.

title: POST /mcp logs all request headers (bearer token, x-n8n-key) and the full JSON body before authentication
reason: At the default info level, every POST /mcp writes the Authorization bearer token, each tenant's x-n8n-key n8n API key, and the whole JSON-RPC body (including n8n_manage_credentials create/update `data` secrets) to stdout/container logs; it runs outside the ConsoleManager wrapper so it is not suppressed. Anyone with log access gets the server token and every tenant's n8n key and credential values, contradicting the tool's 'never logged' promise.
fix: Remove headers and bodyContent from this log line (log method, sessionId and a redacted header list only), or move it to debug with Authorization, x-n8n-key and params.arguments.data redacted.

title: Model can create, activate and trigger arbitrary n8n workflows with no approval step
reason: By design, n8n_create_workflow / n8n_update_partial_workflow (activateWorkflow) / n8n_test_workflow let any tool call build a workflow with Code, HTTP Request or Execute Command nodes, activate it and fire it, so a prompt injection can run code or send data out from the n8n instance using its stored credentials. The only controls are the operator-set DISABLED_TOOLS list, the n8n API key scope and the client honouring destructiveHint annotations.
fix: Document running with DISABLED_TOOLS for write/activate/test tools unless needed, require client-side approval for these tools, and use an n8n API key scoped to a sandbox project; consider refusing to activate workflows containing Code/Execute Command nodes without an explicit confirm flag.

title: Destructive delete actions run immediately with no confirmation or dry-run
reason: n8n_delete_workflow and n8n_manage_credentials action=delete permanently delete on the first call; a prompt-injected call can wipe workflows or credentials. Only the destructiveHint annotation (client-dependent) stands in the way.
fix: Require a confirm: true argument echoed back from a preview call, or keep these tools in DISABLED_TOOLS by default.

title: Execution data and workflow/template content returned raw to the model
reason: n8n_executions get returns execution data, which contains whatever external webhooks, emails or HTTP responses the workflow processed, straight into the model context unmarked; combined with M002 this is the path for injected instructions.
fix: Mark returned execution/template content as untrusted data and default to summary/metadata modes.
